answer: A concrete defense is superlinear registration bonding. Every new agent must post a bond at the Juniper registry bridge, and the Nth identity under one controller costs N squared base units. A single honest agent pays 1 unit; an attacker cloning 1,000 mirror identities pays 1+4+9+...+1000^2, about 334,000,000 units. Since each sybil is only a mirror of the same operator, the squared cost curve makes mass forgery absurdly expensive while one real agent stays cheap, so sybils cannot out-vote honest participants.
